Oxygen: Animals consume oxygen, while plants produce it. When oxygen is insufficient in the ecological tank, animal health declines.
Carbon Dioxide: Animals produce carbon dioxide, while plants consume it. When carbon dioxide levels are too high in the ecological tank, animal health declines.
Waste: Animals produce waste, while plants consume it. When waste levels are too high in the ecological tank, the health of both animals and plants declines.
Vegetarian Food: Food for herbivores. When food is insufficient, animal health declines.

Congratulations on having your own desktop ecological tank, let's work together for the ecological balance in the tank!
But now the ecological tank is empty and worrying.
How about we go field collecting some animals and plants to put in the ecological tank first.
There seem to be many places for field collecting, to be cautious let's start from nearby places first.
Fortunately the outskirts are close enough that we don't need to spend money to go there.
Great! We seem to have collected quite a few interesting animals and plants.
Let's open it and see what we got.
Since we have gains, let's put them in the ecological tank.
Items we get from field collecting are first stored in the warehouse, making it convenient for us to arrange them further.
Let's go check out the warehouse first.
Besides animals and plants, decorations and blocks are also stored in the warehouse. Remember to visit the warehouse often in the future.
Let's put the plants we collected into the ecological tank first.
Let's put the other one in too.
Plants are also an important part of the ecosystem. They not only produce oxygen, but also vegetarian food.
They can also consume excess carbon dioxide and waste in the ecological tank, but plants themselves need nutrition to stay vital.
More importantly, plants can beautify our ecological tank. Let's place this plant in the ecological tank.
Now you can choose where to place the plant in the ecological tank.
You can change the placement position using keyboard [W][A][S][D][Z][X].
When you've chosen the position, press keyboard [Space] to confirm the placement. Then the task of placing plants is up to you.
As you know, an ecosystem has many attributes that need to be balanced for the animals and plants to grow and reproduce.
So we need to always pay attention to the various attributes in the ecological tank, keeping them all in a healthy state.
Vegetarian food is the food for herbivores. This is very important, let's feed some now.
Nutrition is equally important. If the nutrition in the ecological tank is insufficient, plants will lose the ability to maintain ecological balance. Let's add some too.
Do you find it boring to always look at the ecological tank from a fixed angle?
Then let's try adjusting the angle.
Here you can not only adjust the angle, but also change the position of the ecological tank on the desktop. Feel free to try everything.

Paracheirodon axelrodi, order Characiformes, family Characidae, genus Paracheirodon. Native to the Amazon River Basin in South America. Body length 4-5 cm, spindle-shaped, laterally compressed, with shallow arc-shaped dorsal and ventral margins.

Paracheirodon innesi, order Characiformes, family Characidae, genus Paracheirodon. Native to the Amazon River Basin in South America. Body length 4-5 cm, spindle-shaped, laterally compressed, with shallow arc-shaped dorsal and ventral margins.

Trigonostigma heteromorpha, order Cypriniformes, family Cyprinidae, genus Trigonostigma. Native to Thailand, Malaysia, and Indonesia. Body length 4-6 cm, spindle-shaped, slightly laterally compressed, with a forked tail fin.

Danio rerio, order Cypriniformes, family Cyprinidae, genus Danio. Native to streams in Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, Myanmar, and Nepal. Body length 4-5 cm, spindle-shaped, with a long, forked tail fin.

Puntigrus tetrazona, order Cypriniformes, family Cyprinidae. Native to Indonesia and Malaysia. Body length 4-5 cm, high-bodied, laterally compressed, slightly oval-shaped. The body has four thick vertical stripes, resembling a tiger's pattern, hence the name Tiger Barb.

Danio nigrofasciatus, order Cypriniformes, family Cyprinidae, genus Danio. Native to streams in Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, Myanmar, and Nepal. Body length 4-5 cm, spindle-shaped, with a long, forked tail fin.

Pterophyllum scalare, order Cichliformes, family Cichlidae, genus Pterophyllum. Native to the Amazon River Basin. Body length 12-15 cm, flattened body, pointed head, diamond-shaped body, triangular dorsal and anal fins.
Eleocharis parvula, family Cyperaceae, genus Eleocharis. Distributed in Russia, Korea, Japan, India, Myanmar, Vietnam, and China. Numerous stems, fine as hair, densely clustered like felt.
Ludwigia repens, dicotyledonous emergent stem plant. Native to Southeast Asia, now widely distributed in aquarium landscapes worldwide.
Ludwigia palustris, dicotyledonous emergent stem plant. Native to Southeast Asia, now widely distributed in aquarium landscapes worldwide.

Hemianthus callitrichoides, family Scrophulariaceae, dicotyledonous plant, emergent aquatic grass. One of the smallest aquatic plants, discovered in Havana, Cuba. Emersed and submerged forms are similar.

In the ecological tank, animals consume food and oxygen while producing carbon dioxide and waste. Plants, on the other hand, produce food and oxygen while consuming carbon dioxide and waste, thus creating an ecological balance between animals and plants.
Multiple ecological tanks can be created, each being an independent ecosystem.

Depending on the size of the ecological tank, the available space varies. Animals will only reproduce and can be placed from the warehouse into the ecological tank when there is sufficient space. Additionally, the space required by each animal differs.

Travel to various locations worldwide to collect animals and plants. Each location has its own unique flora and fauna. New decorations, devices, ecological tanks, etc., can also be obtained from these locations.
Various animals can be raised in the ecological tank. They grow and reproduce, increasing the number of animals in the tank.

Each animal species has a tolerance level for the environment. When the ecological tank's environment fails to meet an animal's living requirements, its health gradually declines until death. If the environment improves, the animal's health will gradually recover.
Each animal has a quality level determined by its parents. Higher-quality animals can be sold for better prices.
When two adult animals of the same species are present in the tank, they will reproduce.

When an animal dies, it consumes oxygen more rapidly and produces more carbon dioxide and waste. Therefore, dead animals often worsen the tank's environment. Remember to remove dead animals from the ecological tank early.

Plants release oxygen and remove carbon dioxide and waste from the ecological tank, thereby maintaining ecological balance. Plants grow over time, and their ability to maintain ecological balance gradually improves.

Plants consume nutrition. When nutrition is insufficient in the ecological tank, plants cease metabolism and cannot maintain ecological balance. Therefore, it is essential to monitor nutrition levels in the tank regularly.
Various devices can be installed in the ecological tank to stabilize the ecological balance.
Adjust the position and angle of each ecological tank under the "Adjust Size" option in the ecological tank information interface for the best viewing angle.
